seo_title: Delhi HC Shields Taxmann's Headnotes as Copyright
title: Delhi High Court Restrains Publisher From Reproducing Taxmann's Headnotes in Eight Tax Law Books
case_name: Taxmann Allied Services Pvt. Ltd. v. Commercial Law Publishers (India) Pvt. Ltd. & Ors.
card_summary: The Delhi High Court granted Taxmann an ex parte ad interim injunction against Commercial Law Publishers and the authors of eight income tax titles, restraining sale of those books. Justice Vikas Mahajan found prima facie that hundreds of headnotes in the books were verbatim reproductions of Taxmann's own headnotes, which the court held are a literary work protected under the Copyright Act, 1957.
card_tip: A legal or tax publisher should record the editorial judgment behind its own headnotes and treat a rival publisher's headnotes as protected text, since verbatim copying can draw an ex parte injunction before a hearing.
verification_notes: The case name, CS(COMM) 1133/2026, the 2 November 2026 date, Justice Vikas Mahajan on the bench, the eight-book scope, the finding of verbatim copying of hundreds of headnotes, and the Copyright Act, 1957 reasoning on original literary works are reported consistently by LiveLaw Biz, Verdictum and TaxGuru (also Lawchakra and Courtbook, not cited, to keep the source list to three). This is an interim, ex parte order; the defendants have not yet been heard and the suit has not been decided on merits, which the card states. One source adds that the defendants' books credited 'TAXMANN.COM' as a source, cited by Taxmann as evidence of awareness; this detail was seen in only one source and is omitted from the card fields.
